correctness.rationale: The exact curvature-squared formula follows from moving-frame derivatives of the declared trefoil. Differentiation reduces its cosine derivative to 8F_R/V^4. Under y=(1+c)/(1-c), the six explicit transformed coefficients have an ordered, single-sign-change structure: two are positive, and the remaining four each have one positive R-1 root in disjoint rational intervals. Descartes rule gives exactly one interior cosine critical point for 1<R<R*, and none for R>=R*. Boundary signs classify all strict extrema, including the unique inflection-radius curvature-zero minimum. Implicit differentiation and cos(3t) expansion prove quartic flattening and square-root splitting. Standard-library arithmetic and direct 3D vector checks succeeded. Finite checks are corroboration, not a substitute for the exact sign proof.

The other full-text comparator studies contact-constrained elastic knots, not fixed torus parametrizations. Targeted bibliographic queries and available published mathematical-result comparisons did not identify an equivalent or stronger theorem. This is provisional historical priority, not certification.
residual_risks: Historical priority is provisional: an older unindexed computation or a thesis could have computed the same sharp vertex threshold.

value.rationale: The standard circular trefoil is a canonical realization of the simplest nontrivial knot; its curvature extrema describe localized bending geometry. The theorem completely classifies all strict curvature extrema for every embedded ring-torus aspect, detects a threshold far below the previously established inflection aspect and proves a square-root peak-merger normal form. This is a natural complete shape bifurcation, not an arbitrary isolated parameter computation. No broader knot-energy or all-torus-knot theorem is claimed.
